text: {"overall_winner":"A","qualities":[{"evidence":"three body paragraphs with a clear opening and closing question","quality":"organization","description":"The essay is divided into distinct sections that make the argument easier to follow from introduction through conclusion."},{"evidence":"“Though, will we still have control?” / “So why not drive yourself?” / “who is to blame?”","quality":"rhetorical questioning","description":"The essay uses questions to engage the reader and push its argument instead of only stating claims."},{"evidence":"“The percent of laziness in the world is very high therefore, the probability of this car being the top seller, is also high.”","quality":"argumentative development","description":"The essay offers more extended reasoning that tries to explain why driverless cars might or might not succeed."},{"evidence":"“So while you are watching the road the car is watching you.”","quality":"use of source details","description":"The essay incorporates specific information from the article and connects it to its own position."},{"evidence":"“You put your life in the hands of a robot, then when something happens and you die, who is to blame?”","quality":"concluding emphasis","description":"The ending returns to the main concern and leaves the reader with a focused final warning."}]}
